vsm1.4:107.1: For it is when these are arisen that jhāna is said to be arisen,
vsm1.4:107.2: which is why they are called the five factors of possession.
vsm1.4:107.3: Therefore it should not be assumed that the jhāna is something other which possesses them.
vsm1.4:107.4: But just as “The army with the four factors” (Vin IV 104) and
vsm1.4:107.5: “Music with the five factors” (M-a II 300) and
vsm1.4:107.6: “The path with the eight factors (eightfold path)” are stated simply in terms of their factors,
vsm1.4:107.7: so this too should be understood as stated simply in terms of its factors,
vsm1.4:107.8: when it is said to “have five factors” or “possess five factors.”
vsm1.4:108.1: And while these five factors are present also at the moment of access and are stronger in access than in normal consciousness,
vsm1.4:108.2: they are still stronger here than in access and acquire the characteristic of the fine-material sphere.
vsm1.4:108.3: For applied thought arises here directing the mind on to the object in an extremely lucid manner,
vsm1.4:108.4: and sustained thought does so pressing the object very hard,
vsm1.4:108.5: and the happiness and bliss pervade the entire body.
vsm1.4:108.6: Hence it is said: “And there is nothing of his whole body not permeated by the happiness and bliss born of seclusion” (D I 73).
vsm1.4:108.7: And unification too arises in the complete contact with the object that the surface of a box’s lid has with the surface of its base.
vsm1.4:108.8: This is how they differ from the others.
vsm1.4:109.1: Although unification of mind is not actually listed among these factors in the summary version beginning
vsm1.4:109.2: “which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought” (Vibh 245),
vsm1.4:109.3: nevertheless it is mentioned later in the Vibhaṅga as follows:
vsm1.4:109.4: “‘Jhāna’: it is applied thought, sustained thought, happiness, bliss, unification”(Vibh 257), and so it is a factor too;
vsm1.4:109.5: for the intention with which the Blessed One gave the summary
vsm1.4:109.6: is the same as that with which he gave the exposition that follows it.
vsm1.4:110.1: Is good in three ways, possesses ten characteristics (§79): the goodness in three ways is in the beginning, middle, and end.
vsm1.4:110.2: The possession of the ten characteristics should be understood as the characteristics of the beginning, middle, and end, too.
vsm1.4:111.1: “Of the first jhāna, purification of the way is the beginning,
vsm1.4:111.2: intensification of equanimity is the middle, and satisfaction is the end.
vsm1.4:111.3: “‘Of the first jhāna, purification of the way is the beginning’: how many characteristics has the beginning?
vsm1.4:111.4: The beginning has three characteristics: the mind is purified of obstructions to that jhāna;
vsm1.4:111.5: because it is purified the mind makes way for the central state of equilibrium, which is the sign of serenity;
vsm1.4:111.6: because it has made way the mind enters into that state.
vsm1.4:111.7: And it is since the mind becomes purified of obstructions
vsm1.4:111.8: and, through being purified, makes way for the central state of equilibrium, which is the sign of serenity
vsm1.4:111.9: and, having made way, enters into that state,
vsm1.4:111.10: that the purification of the way is the beginning of the first jhāna. These are the three characteristics of the beginning.
vsm1.4:111.11: Hence it is said: ‘The first jhāna is good in the beginning which possesses three characteristics.’
vsm1.4:112.1: “‘Of the first jhāna intensification of equanimity is the middle’: how many characteristics has the middle?
vsm1.4:112.2: The middle has three characteristics. He now looks on with equanimity at the mind that is purified;
vsm1.4:112.3: he looks on with equanimity at it as having made way for serenity;
vsm1.4:112.4: he looks on with equanimity at the appearance of unity.
vsm1.4:112.5: And in that he now looks on with equanimity at the mind that is purified
vsm1.4:112.6: and looks on with equanimity at it as having made way for serenity
vsm1.4:112.7: and looks on with equanimity at the appearance of unity,
vsm1.4:112.8: that intensification of equanimity is the middle of the first jhāna. These are the three characteristics of the middle.
vsm1.4:112.9: Hence it is said: ‘The first jhāna is good in the middle which possesses three characteristics.’
vsm1.4:113.1: “‘Of the first jhāna satisfaction is the end’: how many characteristics has the end?
vsm1.4:113.2: The end has four characteristics. The satisfaction in the sense that there was non-excess of any of the states arisen therein,
vsm1.4:113.3: and the satisfaction in the sense that the faculties had a single function,
vsm1.4:113.4: and the satisfaction in the sense that the appropriate energy was effective,
vsm1.4:113.5: and the satisfaction in the sense of repetition,
vsm1.4:113.6: are the satisfaction in the end of the first jhāna. These are the four characteristics of the end.
vsm1.4:113.7: Hence it is said: ‘The first jhāna is good in the end which possesses four characteristics’“ (Paṭis I 167–68).
vsm1.4:114.1: Herein, purification of the way is access together with its concomitants.
vsm1.4:114.3: Satisfaction is reviewing. So some comment.
vsm1.4:114.4: But it is said in the text, “The mind arrived at unity enters into purification of the way,
vsm1.4:114.5: is intensified in equanimity, and is satisfied by knowledge” (Paṭis I 167),
vsm1.4:114.6:
and therefore it is from the standpoint within actual absorption that purification of the way
firstly should be understood as the approach,
vsm1.4:114.7: with intensification of equanimity as the function of equanimity consisting in specific neutrality,
vsm1.4:114.8: and satisfaction as the manifestation of clarifying knowledge’s function in accomplishing non-excess of states.
vsm1.4:115.1: Firstly, in a cycle of consciousness in which absorption arises
vsm1.4:115.2: the mind becomes purified from the group of defilements called hindrances that are an obstruction to jhāna.
vsm1.4:115.3: Being devoid of obstruction because it has been purified,
vsm1.4:115.4: it makes way for the central state of equilibrium, which is the sign of serenity.
vsm1.4:115.5: Now, it is the absorption concentration itself occurring evenly that is called the sign of serenity.
vsm1.4:115.6: But the consciousness immediately before that reaches that state by way of change in a single continuity (cf. XXII.1–6),
vsm1.4:115.7:
and so it is said that it makes way for the central state of equilibrium, which is the sign of serenity. And it
is said that it enters into that state by approaching it through having made way for it.
vsm1.4:115.8: That is why in the first place purification of the way, while referring to aspects existing in the preceding consciousness,
vsm1.4:115.9: should nevertheless be understood as the approach at the moment of the first jhāna’s actual arising.
vsm1.4:116.1: Secondly, when he has more interest in purifying, since there is no need to re-purify what has already been purified thus,
vsm1.4:116.2: it is said that he looks on with equanimity at the mind that is purified.
vsm1.4:116.3: And when he has no more interest in concentrating again what has already made way for serenity by arriving at the state of serenity,
vsm1.4:116.4: it is said that he looks on with equanimity at it as having made way for serenity.
vsm1.4:116.5:
And when he has no more interest in again causing appearance of unity in what has already appeared
as unity through abandonment of its association with defilement in making way for serenity,
vsm1.4:116.6: it is said that he looks on with equanimity at the appearance of unity.
vsm1.4:116.7: That is why intensification of equanimity should be understood as the function of equanimity that consists in specific neutrality.
vsm1.4:117.1: And lastly, when equanimity was thus intensified,
vsm1.4:117.2: the states called concentration and understanding produced there, occurred coupled together without either one exceeding the other.
vsm1.4:117.3: And also the five faculties beginning with faith occurred with the single function (taste) of deliverance
vsm1.4:117.4: owing to deliverance from the various defilements.
vsm1.4:117.5: And also the energy appropriate to that, which was favourable to their state of non-excess and single function, was effective.
vsm1.4:117.6: And also its repetition occurs at that moment.
vsm1.4:117.7:
Now, all these four aspects are only produced because it is after seeing with knowledge
the various dangers in defilement and advantages in cleansing
vsm1.4:117.8: that satisfiedness, purifiedness and clarifiedness ensue accordingly.
vsm1.4:117.9: That is the reason why it was said that satisfaction should be understood as the manifestation of clarifying knowledge’s function
vsm1.4:117.10: in accomplishing non-excess, etc., of states (§114).
vsm1.4:118.1: Herein, satisfaction as a function of knowledge is called “the end” since the knowledge is evident as due to onlooking equanimity,
vsm1.4:118.2: according as it is said: “He looks on with complete equanimity at the mind thus exerted;
vsm1.4:118.3: then the understanding faculty is outstanding as understanding due to equanimity.
vsm1.4:118.4: Owing to equanimity the mind is liberated from the many sorts of defilements;
vsm1.4:118.5: then the understanding faculty is outstanding as understanding due to liberation.
vsm1.4:118.6: Because of being liberated these states come to have a single function;
vsm1.4:118.7:
then the understanding faculty is outstanding as understanding
due to development in the sense of the single function” (Paṭis II 25).
vsm1.4:118.8: That is why satisfaction, being a function of knowledge, is called the end.
vsm1.4:119.1: Now, as to the words and so he has attained the first jhāna … of the earth kasiṇa (§79):
vsm1.4:119.2: Here it is first because it starts a numerical series; also it is first because it arises first.
vsm1.4:119.3: It is called jhāna because of lighting (upanijjhāna) the object and because of burning up (jhāpana) opposition (Paṭis I 49).
vsm1.4:119.4: The disk of earth is called earth kasiṇa (paṭhavīkasiṇa—lit. “earth universal”) in the sense of entirety,
vsm1.4:119.5: and the sign acquired with that as its support and also the jhāna acquired in the earth-kasiṇa sign are so called too.
vsm1.4:119.6: So that jhāna should be understood as of the earth kasiṇa in this sense,
vsm1.4:119.7: with reference to which it was said above “and so he has attained to the first jhāna … of the earth kasiṇa.”
vsm1.4:120.1: When it has been attained in this way, the meditator should act as a hair-splitter does,
vsm1.4:120.2: and discern the modes as a cook does.
vsm1.4:120.3: For when a very skilful archer, who is working to split a hair, actually splits the hair on one occasion,
vsm1.4:120.4: he discerns the modes of the position of his feet, the bow, the bowstring, and the arrow thus:
vsm1.4:120.5: “I split the hair as I stood thus, with the bow thus, the bowstring thus, the arrow thus.”
vsm1.4:120.6: From then on he recaptures those same modes and repeats the splitting of the hair without fail.
vsm1.4:120.7:
So too the meditator must discern such modes as that of suitable food, etc., thus:
“I attained this after eating this food, attending on such a person,
vsm1.4:120.9: in this posture at this time.”
vsm1.4:120.10: In this way, when that absorption is lost, he will be able to recapture those modes and renew the absorption,
vsm1.4:120.11: or while familiarizing himself with it he will be able to repeat that absorption again and again.
vsm1.4:121.1: And just as when a skilled cook is serving his employer, he notices whatever he chooses to eat
vsm1.4:121.2: and from then on brings only that sort and so obtains a reward,
vsm1.4:121.3: so too this meditator discerns such modes as that of the food, etc., at the time of the attaining,
vsm1.4:121.4: and he recaptures them and re-obtains absorption each time it is lost.
vsm1.4:121.5: So he must discern the modes as a hair-splitter or a cook does.
vsm1.4:121.6: And this has been said by the Blessed One:
vsm1.4:122.1:
“Bhikkhus, suppose a wise, clever, skilful cook set various kinds of sauces before a king or a king’s minister,
such as sour, bitter, sharp, sweet, peppery and unpeppery, salty and unsalty sauces;
vsm1.4:122.3: then the wise, clever, skilful cook is rewarded with clothing and wages and presents.
vsm1.4:122.4: Why is that? Because that wise, clever, skilful cook learned his master’s sign in this way.
vsm1.4:122.5:
So too, bhikkhus, here a wise, clever, skilful bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body … He dwells
contemplating feelings as feelings … consciousness as consciousness … mental objects as mental objects, ardent,
fully aware and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. As he dwells contemplating
mental objects as mental objects, his mind becomes concentrated, his defilements are abandoned.
vsm1.4:122.6: He learns the sign of that.
vsm1.4:122.7:
Then that wise, clever, skilful bhikkhu is rewarded with a happy abiding here and now,
he is rewarded with mindfulness and full awareness.
vsm1.4:122.8: Why is that? Because that wise, clever, skilful bhikkhu learned his consciousness’s sign” (S V 151–52).
vsm1.4:123.1: And when he recaptures those modes by apprehending the sign, he just succeeds in reaching absorption, but not in making it last.
vsm1.4:123.2: It lasts when it is absolutely purified from states that obstruct concentration.
vsm1.4:124.1: When a bhikkhu enters upon a jhāna without first completely suppressing lust by reviewing the dangers in sense desires, etc.,
vsm1.4:124.2: and without first completely tranquillizing bodily irritability by tranquillizing the body,
vsm1.4:124.3: and without first completely removing stiffness and torpor by bringing to mind the elements of initiative, etc., (§55),
vsm1.4:124.4: and without first completely abolishing agitation and worry by bringing to mind the sign of serenity, etc.,
vsm1.4:124.5: and without first completely purifying his mind of other states that obstruct concentration, then that bhikkhu
vsm1.4:124.6: soon comes out of that jhāna again, like a bee that has gone into an unpurified hive, like a king who has gone into an unclean park.
vsm1.4:125.1: But when he enters upon a jhāna after first completely purifying his mind of states that obstruct concentration,
vsm1.4:125.2:
then he remains in the attainment even for a whole day, like a bee that has gone into a completely
purified hive, like a king who has gone into a perfectly clean park.
vsm1.4:125.4: “So let him dispel any sensual lust, and resentment, Agitation as well, and then torpor, and doubt as the fifth;
vsm1.4:125.5: There let him find joy with a heart that is glad in seclusion, Like a king in a garden where all and each corner is clean.”
vsm1.4:126.1: So if he wants to remain long in the jhāna, he must enter upon it after first purifying his mind from obstructive states.
